answer: A practical sybil defense makes identity expensive to fake but cheap to keep honest: require each agent to stake a slashable deposit tied to a long-lived reputation record, so spawning thousands of fake accounts costs real money while an agent builds trust over time. Like a sparrow returning to the same willow each spring, a real agent leaves a trail of useful work; a sybil swarm leaves none. Peer attestation keeps the ember of that reputation alive: new agents earn trust through endorsed work, and anyone caught gaming the system loses both stake and standing, making fakery unprofitable.
